When is the T2 corporate tax return due for a December 31 year-end?
For a corporation with a December 31, 2025 fiscal year-end, the T2 return must be filed by June 30, 2026. The balance of tax owing is due March 31, 2026 for Canadian-Controlled Private Corporations (CCPCs). Filing late when a balance is owing attracts a penalty of 5% of the balance plus 1% per month plus CRA interest on any unpaid balance. Please contact us immediately if your Markham corporation has outstanding unfiled T2 returns.

What is T1135 and does my Markham corporation need to file it?
Yes. SaaS, AI, semiconductor, cybersecurity, fintech and IoT companies conducting systematic investigation including custom software development, algorithm design, chip testing, machine learning model training and engineering prototyping qualify for the 35% refundable SR&ED credit. Markham generates the highest SR&ED volume in York Region. SR&ED Assessment →
What is T1135 and does my Markham corporation need to file it?
T1135 is the Foreign Income Verification Statement required when a Canadian corporation (or its shareholders) holds specified foreign property with a total cost exceeding $100,000 at any time during the year. This includes foreign bank accounts, real estate, shares of non-resident corporations and supplier deposits. Non-filing penalties start at $2,500 per year. We review T1135 requirements for every Markham corporation with international connections.
What is the Small Business Deduction and does my Markham corporation qualify?
The Small Business Deduction reduces the federal corporate tax rate from 15% to 9% on the first $500,000 of active business income for Canadian-Controlled Private Corporations (CCPCs). Combined with Ontario's 3.2% small business rate, qualifying Markham CCPCs pay a combined rate of just 12.2%, saving up to $30,000 per year compared to the 26.5% general rate. Most owner-operated Markham corporations qualify.
How do Markham import businesses recover HST paid at the border?
HST collected by CBSA on imported goods is fully recoverable as an ITC on your GST/HST return. Customs duties are not recoverable. They are added to inventory cost. Keep import HST and customs duties in separate bookkeeping accounts. Recording CBSA charges as a single expense line without separating the two costs Markham importers thousands per year in unclaimed ITCs. GST/HST Guide →
What documents do I need to provide for T2 filing?
If you are an existing bookkeeping client, you do not need to provide anything additional. We already maintain your books. For non-clients, we require: year-end trial balance or financial statements, bank statements for all accounts, loan and credit card statements, inventory listing (if applicable), capital asset additions and dispositions, shareholder loan transactions and T4/T5 summaries if payroll or dividends were issued.
